package_info.package_versions: Outdated Magento CMS versions on 80 e-commerce sites
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code on compromised Magento e-commerce sites captures customers’ payment information during checkout and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling credit card theft and fraudulent transactions.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (checkout page load and form submission)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in Magento checkout templates (e.g., app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml or via third-party JS includes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the checkout form submission, reads credit card fields from the DOM, and sends the data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting sensitive payment data and sending it to an external, attacker-controlled server is a classic sign of a skimmer or data exfiltration attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to payment gateways or fraud detection services, but only to vetted, trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Direct access to credit card fields in the DOM
Network requests to untrusted, hardcoded domains
Code injected into checkout templates or loaded from third-party sources

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits outdated Magento CMS to gain write access to e-commerce site files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to inject malicious JavaScript into checkout pages

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into checkout page templates or loaded as a third-party script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in customers’ browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer loads the checkout page and submits payment, the malicious script captures credit card data and exfiltrates it to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment data for fraud or resale

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing payment form fields and sending data to external domains
Unexpected network requests from checkout pages to non-payment domains
Modification of checkout templates or inclusion of unknown third-party scripts
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious JavaScript files in webroot
References to external scripts in checkout page source
network_indicators: POST requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with payment processors
Unusual traffic to newly registered or untrusted domains during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to checkout templates and unexpected third-party JavaScript includes. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for POST requests to unknown domains, especially those containing payment data. Use file integrity monitoring on Magento template files and alert on modifications. Employ web application firewalls to block or alert on suspicious outbound requests from e-commerce pages.
